q: What is the capital of Australia?
x: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise because Sydney and Melbourne both wanted to be the capital.

q: Which planet has the most known moons?
x: Saturn pulled clearly ahead of Jupiter after a batch of discoveries in 2023 and has well over 200 now.

q: Which element has the chemical symbol W?
x: W comes from its other name, wolfram. Tin is Sn.

q: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
x: It's about 0.44 km². Monaco is second.

q: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
x: He painted it from 1508 to 1512, even though he thought of himself as a sculptor.

q: How many bones are in the adult human body?
x: Babies are born with around 300, and many of them fuse as they grow.

q: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
x: It fell on November 9, 1989. Germany reunified in 1990, and the USSR dissolved in 1991.

q: Which country has the largest population?
x: India passed China in 2023, according to UN estimates.

q: Who wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude?
x: It came out in 1967. García Márquez won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982.

q: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
x: About 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

q: What is the largest desert in the world?
x: A desert is defined by low precipitation, not heat. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

q: In what year did the Titanic sink?
x: It sank on April 15, 1912, on its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York.

q: Who was the first person to travel into space?
x: Gagarin orbited Earth on April 12, 1961. Alan Shepard was the first American, three weeks later.

q: Which country has the most islands?
x: Sweden has about 267,000 islands, most of them small and uninhabited.

q: Which blood type is the universal donor for red blood cells?
x: AB positive is the universal recipient.

q: In which sport would you see a “Fosbury Flop”?
x: Dick Fosbury won Olympic gold with it in 1968, and now almost every high jumper uses it.

q: Which U.S. state borders only one other state?
x: Maine's only neighboring state is New Hampshire.

q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
x: Two pump blood through the gills, and one pumps it to the rest of the body.

q: Which Shakespeare play has the line “Out, damned spot!”?
x: Lady Macbeth says it while sleepwalking, trying to wash out blood only she can see.

q: Which language has the most native speakers?
x: English has the most speakers overall once second-language learners are counted.
